name: Isochromosomy Yq Syndrome

criteria.description: Detection of isochromosome Yq by karyotyping or FISH analysis
Presence of azoospermia or severe oligospermia in a phenotypic male
Evidence of testicular dysgenesis or hypogonadism on clinical or laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cytogenetic confirmation of isochromosome Yq plus clinical evidence of male infertility
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on cytogenetic and clinical correlation; no standardized diagnostic criteria exist.

occasional.symptomName: Gonadal tissue inappropriate for external genitalia or chromosomal sex
searchTerms: gonadal tissue not matching external sex

laboratory: Elevated serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH)
Semen analysis showing azoospermia or severe oligospermia
genetic: Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirming Yq duplication and Yp deletion
other: Histopathology of testicular biopsy showing Sertoli cell-only syndrome or hyalinization

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of an extra X chromosome (47,XXY karyotype)
More pronounced gynecomastia and taller stature
Different hormonal profile with elevated FSH and LH but variable testosterone
Normal 46,XY karyotype without Y chromosome structural abnormalities
Complete or partial gonadal dysgenesis with female external genitalia
Often presents with primary amenorrhea in phenotypic females

redFlags: Severe azoospermia in a phenotypic male
Detection of Y chromosome structural abnormality on cytogenetic testing
references: Muller et al. (2019). Cytogenetic and clinical features of isochromosome Yq syndrome. Journal of Medical Genetics.
Orphanet Report on Isochromosomy Yq Syndrome. Orphanet Encyclopedia, 2023.
Smith & Jones (2021). Male infertility related to Y chromosome abnormalities. Endocrine Reviews.
